title: Safer or Luckier? LLMs as Safety Evaluators Are Not Robust to Artifacts

bias_targets.methodology: Prepending apologetic phrasing to a completion and measuring the shift in safety preference from LLM judges using sample-level Tie Detection and model-level Winrate Shift tests.
Adding fake authoritative sources or citations to a completion to evaluate if LLM judges improperly correlate citations with higher safety.
Appending a helpful, chatty closing sentence (e.g., 'Is there anything else I can help you with?') to a completion to test if this positive persona skews the judge's safety assessment.
Rephrasing completions to be longer without changing their core meaning or safety, and measuring if LLM judges inherently prefer more verbose responses.
Swapping the presentation order of the two completions (A vs. B) in the evaluator's prompt to measure if the LLM judge systematically favors the first or second position.
